Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: Patients with cognitive impairment had lower NPI dysphoria/depression scores (fewer symptoms) than cognitively normal patients.
Sentence: "On the NPI, the CI group had significantly lower scores (indicating fewer symptoms) than the CN group across all 12 domains, including delusions, hallucinations, agitation/aggression, dysphoria/depression, anxiety, elation/euphoria, apathy/indifference, disinhibition, irritability/lability, aberrant motor activity, nighttime behaviours/sleep disturbances, and appetite/eating disorders, as well as higher total NPI scores (p < 0.05)."
Measured as: NPI dysphoria/depression domain score
Population: Patients with ESRD undergoing maintenance haemodialysis
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Cognitively normal group vs cognitively impaired group
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 132
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation reduced depression severity (BDI-II) more than placebo in patients with mild to moderate depression.
Sentence: "At the end point, statistically significant changes were observed only in intervention group as compared with controls including increased 25(OH)D concentration (+ 40.83 ± 28.57 vs. + 5.14 ± 23.44 nmol L-1, P < 0.001) and decreased depression severity (-11.75 ± 6.40 vs. -3.61 ± 10.40, P = 0.003)."
Measured as: depression severity (Beck Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 56 patients aged 18-60 years with mild to moderate depression
Intervention: cholecalciferol 50,000 IU every 2 weeks for 8 weeks
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 56
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A compares cognitively impaired vs normal haemodialysis patients on NPI scores, so vitamin D is only a measured covariate, not the exposure, while Study B is a vitamin D supplementation trial.","verdict":"off_question","reason":null,"also_differs":[],"detail":"exposure: cognitive impairment status (CI vs CN) in haemodialysis patients, not vitamin D"}
